slice: Triumph TF pass 6: gap fill for aftermarket exhausts, clutch, suspension, clamps, protection, brakes, drivetrain, wheels and tester feedback (2024-2027)

products.product: 2024-2025 Triumph TF KYB Pro Fork Revalve
products.variants: Send-in service; a DIY kit version is sold separately

fits.notes: Listed on the 2025 TF 450-RC Edition page

products.what_it_changes: Maker copy: fork revalved to the JBI Spec; settings guide supplied.
products.supporting_parts: Springs sold separately by rider weight (see the JBI spring chart).
products.caveats: No SKU shown. Model coverage given only as 'Triumph TF'; 2026-2027 not listed for the fork.

products.product: 2024-2025 JBI Spec Triumph TF Pro Fork DIY Kit

fits.notes: Listed on the 2025 TF 450-RC Edition page

products.what_it_changes: Do-it-yourself parts kit to bring the KYB fork to the JBI valving spec.
products.caveats: No SKU shown; contents not itemized on the page read.

products.product: 2024-2026 JBI Spec Triumph TF Pro Shock DIY Kit

fits.notes: Listed on the 2025 TF 450-RC Edition page

products.what_it_changes: DIY kit version of the JBI shock revalve. The send-in shock revalve ($455, labour, parts and oil) uses a JBI titanium compression piston, titanium piston post and JBI Spec Ti spring plate.
products.caveats: No SKU. The shock revalve page title says 2024-2026 but its metadata says 2024-2025. Which TF models (X, C, E, 450-X) beyond those named is not stated.

products.product: Fork and shock spring rates, 2025 Triumph TF 450-RC Edition
products.variants: Fork 4.5-5.4 N/mm; shock 50-64 N/mm, chosen by rider weight and terrain (MX, soft moto/desert, flowy single track, technical/hard enduro)
products.what_it_changes: Maker chart: stock rates are fork 5.0 N (0.51 kg/mm, 498 mm long) and shock 58 N (260 mm long), suited to a 170-185 lb rider for motocross. Chart MX picks: 120-135 lb 4.7/52; 135-155 lb 4.8/54; 155-170 lb 4.9/56; 170-185 lb 5.0/58 (stock); 185-200 lb 5.1/60; 200-215 lb 5.2/62; 215-230 lb 5.3/63; 230-245 lb 5.4/63-64; 245-275 lb 5.4/64. Weights are in casual clothing; chart applies to stock or modified valving.
products.caveats: Spring SKUs and prices not shown (main listing shows $0.00, a placeholder).

products.product: Revalve, Fork Service (Triumph TF250X / TF450RC)
products.what_it_changes: Send-in fork revalve service.
products.caveats: REVALVEF is the service code used for all bikes on this application page, not a Triumph-specific part. No shock revalve line for Triumph found on this page. 2026-2027 models and TF 450-X/C not listed.

products.product: ROCS Tech Black (22mm offset) Triple Clamps, Triumph TF 250 X (24-25)
products.what_it_changes: Seller copy: opposing clamp system to reduce fork-tube deformation in the clamping area so the fork responds more freely; opposing pinch bolts do not influence each other.
products.caveats: UK retailer listing; maker page not read. Whether tax is included is not stated. 2026-2027 and TF 450 fitment not stated on this page.

products.product: ROCS Pro (20-22mm offset) Triple Clamps, Triumph TF 250 X (24-25)
products.what_it_changes: Seller copy: opposing clamp system to reduce fork-tube deformation; adjustable offset.
products.caveats: Another retailer (Motostorm, Italy) lists the same number as 'XT-40601005 ROCS Kit M12 Triple Clamps (Triumph TF 250-X 24)' with 2024-2026 fitment; product naming conflicts between retailers. Maker page not read.

products.product: Skid Plate HDPE 6mm, Triumph TF 250 X (2024-2026) / TF 450-RC (2025-2026), Black
products.what_it_changes: Maker: protects frame, lower engine, water pump and cases; HDPE claimed 30-40% lighter than aluminium and returns to shape after impacts.
products.supporting_parts: Mounting hardware, screws, instructions and sticker included.
products.caveats: Price includes tax (EUR 82.50 before tax). Page says it 'only fits the Triumph TF 250 X / TF 450-RC'; TF 450-X not listed.

products.product: Skid Plate Hard Enduro HDPE 8mm with linkage guard, Triumph TF 450-E / TF 450-RC (2025-2026), Black
products.variants: Black; 8 mm HDPE, 16 mm at linkage; 1.5 kg
products.what_it_changes: Maker: covers frame down to the footpegs, front and side of the water pump and engine cases, with reinforced linkage protection.
products.supporting_parts: Mounts, screws, instructions and sticker included.
products.caveats: Price includes tax (EUR 132.50 before tax). Title names 450-E/RC; the compatibility table adds TF 450 C. TF 450-X not listed.

products.product: TF250 C/E/X 24-26 RS12 Full Exhaust / Aluminum Muffler
products.variants: Stainless full system, aluminium RS-12 muffler

fits.notes: TF250 C/E/X 24-26 (the 250-C was not sold in 2024; years as stated by maker)
TF250 C/E/X 24-26 (years as stated by maker)

products.what_it_changes: Full stainless system with RS-12 aluminium muffler (maker repack chart: REPACK-RS12-MX, 1000 g packing; SA-21-K spark arrester; INS-30-K insert included with system, INS-39-K listed as an option).
products.supporting_parts: Sound inserts INS-30-K (1.500 in), INS-32-K (1.375 in), INS-33-K (1.250 in), INS-34-K (1.250 in SP); repack REPACK-RS12-MX; end cap YM1-CFR-K-1.
products.caveats: Part number taken from the maker product URL and repack chart (no labelled SKU field). Maker lists 24-26 for all three 250 models; 2027 TF 250-X not listed. Whether it fits the 2026+ TF 250-X with its revised airbox/silencer is implied by the 24-26 range but not discussed.

products.product: TF450 25-26 RS12 Full Exhaust / Aluminum Muffler
products.variants: Stainless full system, aluminium RS-12 muffler
products.what_it_changes: Full stainless system with RS-12 aluminium muffler. Repack chart: REPACK-RS12-MX (1000 g), SA-21-K spark arrester, INS-30-K included, INS-YM1-150-SP32 listed (code may be truncated in the chart).
products.caveats: Maker names only 'TF450 25-26'; which TF 450 variants (RC, X, C, E) are covered is not stated. Part number from product URL and chart.

products.product: RS-12 Sound Insert Kits 1.375 / 1.250 / 1.250 SP and Premium MX Repack Kit (Triumph TF250 collection)
products.what_it_changes: Smaller-diameter inserts reduce sound output for the RS-12 muffler; repack kit restores muffler packing.
products.caveats: Fitment only by placement in the Triumph collection; product titles are generic RS-12. Repack chart also lists REPACK-RS12-MX for the TF450 system.

products.product: Factory 4.1 RCT Titanium Anodized Full System w/ Carbon End Cap (Triumph TF 450)
products.what_it_changes: Maker: titanium MegaBomb header and midpipe, shorter muffler set closer to the engine to centralise mass; 'massive power gains' and 'huge weight savings' claimed without figures. Spark-arrester screen and AMA-compliant quiet insert included.
products.caveats: Closed course use only. Listed sold out. Page data shows a lower compare-at price (USD 714.99) that looks like an error. 2027 not listed.

products.product: Stainless Steel / Aluminium Factory 4.1 RCT Full System w/ Carbon Cap (Triumph TF 250)
products.what_it_changes: Maker: stainless MegaBomb header and midpipe, grey anodised aluminium muffler with carbon cap and RTS (Rapid Tuning System); weight stated 13 lb; spark-arrester screen and AMA-compliant quiet insert included.
products.caveats: Closed course use only. Listed sold out. Compare-at price (USD 545.99) on the page looks like an error. 2027 TF 250-X not listed.

products.product: RadiusX 4.0 Clutch (DDS) - Triumph TF450
products.what_it_changes: Automatic (centrifugal) clutch replacing the stock clutch internals; no stall, no clutch needed at stops.
products.caveats: TF 450-X is not in the maker's model list for this kit. Kit contents and cover requirement not stated on the page.

products.product: Clutch Cover - Triumph TF 450-X (2024+)
products.what_it_changes: Replacement clutch cover (Rekluse covers typically add clearance for their auto clutches; not stated on the listing read).
products.caveats: Maker says 'TF 450-X (2024+)' although the TF 450 range began in 2025; only the category listing was read, so fitment to the RC, C and E is not confirmed.

products.product: Replacement Clutch Pack - RadiusCX 4.0 - TF450 25+
products.what_it_changes: Service pack for a RadiusCX 4.0 auto clutch on the TF 450, which implies Rekluse sells a RadiusCX for the TF 450 (kit page not read).
products.caveats: Listing names only 'TF450 25+', no make or variant. Only the category page was read.

products.product: Skid Plate for Triumph (6 mm, integrated linkage fin)
products.what_it_changes: Maker: 6 mm plastic plate for frame and engine, integrated fin protecting the shock linkage from impacts, mud and sand, extended coverage of side cases, valve-adjust cover and footrest area; cut-outs for weight, ventilation and washing; mounts with two supplied screws on original mounts.
products.supporting_parts: Two screws supplied; uses original mounts.
products.caveats: The 10-digit number 2986920001 is shown unlabelled on the maker page (US retailers list it as the part number). No price on the maker page. TF 250-C and TF 450-C not listed. Material stated as 96% plastic, 4% steel; made in Italy.

products.product: Flame Series Fixed Disc 260 mm, front
products.variants: 260.0 mm OD, 126.5 mm ID, 3.1 mm thick, 6 holes x 6.5 mm on 143.0 mm pitch; left side mount
products.what_it_changes: Stock-size (260 mm) fixed replacement front rotor in Moto-Master's Flame pattern; same size as the Galfer OEM 260 mm disc.
products.caveats: Fixed (not floating) disc; maker also lists the same disc for many KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas models. TF 450-X and 2027 models not listed. Price not stated.

products.product: Pressure Spring Set (KYB fork)
products.what_it_changes: Replacement pressure (base-valve/compression-assembly) spring set for the KYB fork; the page gives no spec beyond 'Pressure Spring Set'.
products.caveats: Same code for all four Triumph lines. 2026 TF 250-X/C, TF 450-X/C and 2027 not listed. Function inferred from the product name only.

feedback.product: Owner setup: springs, revalve, gearing 13/52, Renthal 839 Fatbar

bike.year: not stated (2025 build implied by July 2025 post at 16 h)

feedback.publication: Vital MX forum: 'Triumph TF450 reviews and setup tips'
feedback.author: Smith246
feedback.conditions: About 95 kg B-level motocross rider; 16 hours on the bike; came from 2023 YZ450F and 2024 KX450.
feedback.observed: Bike 'much more fun' after changes; noted a rich stutter off the bottom and very stiff upshifts. Later post (2025-11-07): runs 5.2 springs, stock oil-pump gears with no problems, says KTM levers should fit.
feedback.measured: Gearing 13/48 to 13/52 (two links added, axle at rear); shock spring up two rates with stock valving; fork spring up one rate and revalved; sag 102-104 mm; fork tubes 2.5 mm through the clamps; Deep Sand map.
feedback.other_mods: Renthal 839 Fatbar replacing ODI RC-bend bar.

feedback.product: Owner long-term setup: clickers, sag, 13/50 gearing, MX3S front
feedback.publication: Vital MX forum: 'Triumph TF450 reviews and setup tips'
feedback.author: crc245
feedback.conditions: 185 lb rider, Southern California, 30+ A-level speed; long-term test bike at 17.2 hours.
feedback.observed: Prefers Sand-Wet map, suggests trying Expert and RC Signature. Does not run quickshifter or traction control. Rear brake pedal spring came loose at 8 h; seat cover torn. Advises checking spokes often in the first 10 h.
feedback.measured: Fork C15 / R14; shock HSC 7-8, LSC 14, R 11; fork height 2.5 mm; sag 100-102 mm with 26 mm free sag (suggests stiffer rear spring needed, not changed); gearing 13/48 with 114-link chain changed to 13/50 with 116 links; spoke wrench 6.5 mm; Maxima Pro+ 10W-50 oil.
feedback.other_mods: Front tire Dunlop MX34 changed to MX3S; rear kept 110/90-19.

feedback.product: Stock suspension: sag, fork height suggestion, maps
feedback.author: Will Embree
feedback.conditions: One day at Triumph's private tracks near Atlanta, Georgia: slick red clay in the morning, wetter and muddier second track later; 165 lb rider.
feedback.observed: Plush but slightly soft for the rider, mainly the fork on jump landings (suggested a few compression clicks, not tested). Bike pushed the bars in corners; suggested raising the fork 1-2 mm in the clamps (not tested). Standard map 'snappy'; RC map more controllable and linear; Loamy-Wet the softest initial hit. Dunlop MX34 tracked well on slick clay; Brembo brakes strong all day.
feedback.measured: Sag 100 mm (Triumph recommendation). Article reports Carmichael runs the fork at 6 mm and wanted 7 mm. MX Tune Pro offers 11 factory maps.
feedback.other_mods: Stock RC Edition (Neken clamps, ODI bar, holeshot device, Hinson clutch cover, gripper seat).

feedback.product: Maps, traction control and gearing at the Australian launch
feedback.author: Dan Thomerson
feedback.conditions: Australian launch at Ride Park Victoria; new, tight gearboxes; jumps and sandy rollers.
feedback.observed: Stock maps smooth and linear with punchy mid-to-top; Ricky Carmichael map preferred for stronger low-end torque. Traction control kept drive with limited slip out of corners and off jumps. Quickshifter used 2nd-5th nearly all day. Suspension absorbed big jumps and sandy rollers; brakes strong and fade-free.
feedback.measured: Final drive 13/50 (spec sheet); traction control adjustable 1-10 in the app; no clicker or sag numbers given.

feedback.product: Stock suspension and maps, follow-up test at Glen Helen
feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen during MotoFest 2025 (fast downhills, sharp edges), following an earlier wet Georgia clay session.
feedback.observed: KYB softer than expected, suited to a 170 lb intermediate rider. Front rides high in its stroke, allowing more rear preload than expected. Standard map too soft on bottom end and traction control made it softer; Carmichael map 2 sharper, especially low in the rpm. Most riders turned the quickshifter off (only helps at wide-open throttle, can hesitate).
feedback.measured: Most test riders liked 100 mm sag. No clicker numbers.

feedback.author: ADBMAG staff
feedback.conditions: First local test in about 42 C heat; comments on tighter tracks such as Maitland. Ridden without touching sag or fork height.
feedback.observed: Stock gearing good on wide flowing tracks but tall on tight tracks (too much time in 2nd); two teeth larger on the rear suggested. Engine linear, tractable, 'closer to a Kawasaki'; fork held up under braking, shock predictable; turns better than a KTM but not like a Honda.
feedback.measured: Article gives stock final drive as 13/49 in one place and 13/48 in another; suggests about 13/50. Rear tire 100/90-19 Pirelli MX32 (RC uses 110/90-19).

feedback.product: Gearbox detailing for false neutrals: polished dogs, ground shift fork, DLC shift-fork shafts

bike.year: not stated (thread refers to 2026 head stays)

feedback.publication: Vital MX forum: 'Some Chassis and suspension work on the Triumph TF450'
feedback.author: lowmass
feedback.conditions: 180 lb expert vet rider; same thread reports FCP race cups, FCP head stays, titanium pivot axle.
feedback.observed: No false neutrals in about 15 hours after polishing gear dogs and pockets, removing machining burrs, grinding a raised mark on the 3-4 shift fork that rubbed the gears and DLC-coating the shift-fork shafts. Found scrubbing-pad material in the gearbox (speculated to be intentional break-in material). Parts lead times about three weeks over about 10 orders.
feedback.measured: DLC coating cost about USD 150. Earlier post (2026-05-14) lists fork 2 mm up, C15 (stock 13), R10, springs 0.51 to 0.48 kg/mm, 350 cc 0W-16 outer-tube oil (stock 310 cc); shock sag 105 mm (axle about 5 mm behind centre), LSC 16, R12, HSC 1 turn out.
feedback.other_mods: FCP race cups, FCP head stays, FCP titanium swingarm pivot axle and two titanium engine-mount bolts.

feedback.author: Andrew Oldar
feedback.conditions: Dirt Rider in-house Dynojet 250i; map not stated.
feedback.observed: Test rider Casey Casper: 'makes adequate power that feels torquier than it actually is, but has a disconnected feel at the right wrist.'
feedback.measured: 39.9 hp and 18.7 lb-ft peak at the rear wheel (rpm not given).

feedback.product: 2026 450 MX baseline suspension settings: TF450-X; aftermarket clamps
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Baseline settings article for 2026 450 MX bikes; rider weight and speed not stated for the Triumph.
feedback.observed: Bike 'soft, it has good comfort but needs to be stiffened a little to feel balanced off throttle.' Good results reported with aftermarket clamps; Ride Engineering or X-Trig clamps suggested to help the front track better off throttle (no part numbers or measurements).
feedback.measured: Fork: spring 4.8 N/mm, height flush to 2 mm, compression 8-9 out, rebound 11 out. Shock: spring 58 N/mm, LSC 9 out, HSC 1.5 turns out, rebound 11 out. Sag not stated.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Baseline settings article for 2026 250 MX bikes; rider weight not stated for the Triumph.
feedback.observed: 'A well balanced bike out of the box', less work to dial in than others in class, but wanted a little more hold-up front and rear under load; chose a 'happy medium hold up/comfort setting'.
feedback.measured: Fork: spring 4.7 N/mm, height 3 mm, compression 8 out, rebound 8 out. Shock: spring 56 N/mm, sag 103 mm, HSC 1 turn out, LSC 7 out, rebound 10 out.

feedback.product: 2026 gearing guide and chassis lengths: TF250-X and TF450-X 13/49
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Gearing guide (2026-05-01) plus recommended chassis-length posts (450: 2026-06-23; 250: 2026-07-07), stock offset.
feedback.observed: Both TF models have 'an excellent engine character' but need more third-gear recovery; one tooth larger on the rear lets the rider reach third sooner or hold it longer and adds response to the smoother roll-on.
feedback.measured: Stock 13/48, recommended 13/49 on both. Chassis posts: TF250-X wheelbase 1502-1504 mm, swingarm length 593-596 mm; TF450-X ('T450-X' in the post) wheelbase 1499-1501 mm, swingarm 590-595 mm; both at 13/49 with 3 mm fork height.

gaps: Exhausts: no Akrapovic aftermarket (non-Triumph-branded) TF system found; Akrapovic supplies Triumph's genuine titanium exhaust. SC-Project's Triumph range lists only road models (no TF). HGS: nothing found. Pro Circuit maker pages not reachable (fetch refused), so 2026-2027 fitment of its TF systems is unconfirmed. FMF and Yoshimura maker pages list up to 2026; no maker lists 2027 yet.

Clutch: Rekluse RadiusX for TF 450 lists C/E/RC (not X); a RadiusCX 4.0 for TF 450 is implied by a replacement pack (753-12003) but its kit page was not read. Hinson TF 450 basket/cover part numbers not found.

Suspension: Factory Connection lists a fork revalve (REVALVEF) and pressure springs for Triumph; Race Tech, Enzo, Pro Circuit and Dialed TF services/parts not found on maker sites in the searches run. Keefer's 2026 TF450-X fork spring (4.8) differs from Ride JBI's stated 2025 RC stock fork rate (5.0); not reconciled.

Clamps: X-Trig number 40601005 is called 'ROCS Pro 20-22mm' by Brook Suspension and 'ROCS Kit M12' by Motostorm; maker page not read. Ride Engineering has a Triumph clamps category but the site refused fetches; Keefer names Ride Engineering clamps for the TF450-X without part numbers. Luxon: nothing found. 2027 TF 250-X gets new Neken clamps (1000PS, 2026-10-01); aftermarket clamp fitment for 2027 not stated anywhere.

Brakes: Galfer is the OE disc supplier (260 front / 220 rear); no Galfer, Braking or EBC TF-specific aftermarket part numbers found on maker pages. Moto-Master lists a 260 mm Flame fixed disc (110298); no Moto-Master oversize MX kit for TF found.

Sprockets: Supersprox 990-pattern rear and JT JTR897 rear list TF fitment on maker pages (already recorded elsewhere); JT lists stock tooth counts 47 (TF250 C/X, TF450 C/RC), 49 (TF450 X 26), 51 (TF250/450 E), which conflict with testers' 13/48 and ADB's 13/49. Supersprox and Talon front sprocket part numbers for TF not found.
Wheels: Haan, Talon, Kite and Excel/Warp 9 TF wheel part numbers not found; Warp 9 has TF 250-X / TF 450-RC menu collections but the pages could not be reached.
Feedback: no 2027 TF 250-X riding test yet (announcement only, on sale October 2026). No MXA, Racer X or Swapmoto TF 450 test page reached. Vital MX owner posts give no model year.
